title: Keith Jackson's P.A.R.K.: An OU Tight End's Gift to Little Rock
question: What nonprofit did former OU tight end Keith Jackson start?
answer: Keith Jackson, OU's All-America tight end from 1984 to 1987, founded P.A.R.K. (Positive Atmosphere Reaches Kids), a Little Rock after-school nonprofit, in 1993.
summary: All-American tight end Keith Jackson (OU 1984-87) founded P.A.R.K., a Little Rock nonprofit that helps at-risk students stay in school and reach college.
body: Keith Jackson came to Norman from Little Rock Parkview High and played tight end for Barry Switzer from 1984 through 1987. In a run-first wishbone, he was a devastating blocker and a big-play threat, finishing with 62 catches for 1,470 yards and 14 touchdowns, an average of 23.7 yards per grab. He was a consensus All-American in 1986 and 1987, and the Sooners went 42-5-1 with the 1985 national title during his four years.

The Philadelphia Eagles took him 13th overall in 1988, and he set an Eagles receptions record with 81 catches as a rookie on his way to NFC Rookie of the Year honors. Over nine NFL seasons with the Eagles, Dolphins and Packers he made six Pro Bowls and won Super Bowl XXXI with Green Bay.

His most lasting work happened back home. Jackson founded Positive Atmosphere Reaches Kids, known as P.A.R.K., in Little Rock in 1993, while he was still an active NFL player. The nonprofit runs after-school and summer programs for junior high and high school students at risk of falling behind, with tutoring, mentoring, recreation and community service aimed at getting them to college.

A 2020 Talk Business & Politics profile reported that 540 students had graduated from P.A.R.K., many of them set to be the first in their families to go to college, and that its board had built an endowment of roughly $12 million. Jackson has also worked as a radio analyst for Arkansas football and entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 2001.
For a player known for big catches, his biggest contribution may be the hundreds of kids he has helped reach the next level.
